questions.prompt: Which property must a correct batched simulator satisfy?
options: Worlds in the batch share their randomized parameters so that memory use stays small.
The batch size must be a power of two so that the memory layout stays aligned for the kernels.
The batch result may differ slightly from per-world results if the batch runs faster.
World i in the batch gives the same trajectory as world i simulated alone; inputs are not mutated.

questions.prompt: Symmetric two-contact PGS with A=[[5,-3],[-3,5]]. Error factor per sweep (c/a)^2. Precision 0.001.
questions.skillLabel: Convergence of an iterative contact solver

questions.prompt: A residual of 1.0 shrinks by a factor 0.2 per sweep. Smallest whole number of sweeps to get below 1e-3.
questions.skillLabel: Convergence of an iterative contact solver

questions.prompt: Central difference of f(x)=x^3 at x=2 with h=0.1. Value, precision 0.001.
One scalar loss and 10,000 policy parameters through a differentiable rollout. Which gradient method is appropriate?
options: Forward-mode AD, one pass per parameter.
Reverse-mode AD: one backward pass for all parameters.
questions.explanation: Reverse mode costs a small multiple of one rollout.

questions.prompt: A ball hits a wall; the outcome (which side it ends on) is decided by a hard contact. What does the gradient of the final position with respect to launch angle look like?
options: Always equal to the finite-difference value for any step size h you choose.
Undefined only for h < 1e-12, and smooth and informative for all larger values.
Always large and positive, because a bigger angle always moves the ball further.
Zero almost everywhere with jumps at the switching angle, so it carries no useful signal.

questions.prompt: Design a comparison of contact-solver settings for a grasping simulation against a reference: reference, settings, metrics, cost and decision rule.
rubric: Defines a reference (smaller step, tight tolerance or analytic) and a set of settings.
Chooses metrics (trajectory RMSE, penetration, energy) and cost (time per step) and plots error vs cost.
States a decision rule (Pareto knee under an error limit) and a check that could reject a setting.
questions.skillLabel: Compare solver settings to a reference
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
